old: Use *porque* to explain why an action has happened. The reason can follow a sentence in the *pretérito perfecto*: *He vuelto porque ha llovido*. The verb after *porque* is conjugated normally.
new: You know *porque* from A1 Unit 2. Now use it to explain why an action has happened: the reason can follow a sentence in the *pretérito perfecto*, as in *He vuelto porque ha llovido*. The verb after *porque* is conjugated normally.
why: porque was taught in A1 Unit 2 (por-que-y-porque); the screen presents it as new

template.prompt: Ask a friend (use tú) why he or she has returned.
Ask a friend (use tú) what he or she thinks of the excursion.
Say that you think it has been fun.

why: 'someone' does not pin tú; 'Say that it has been fun' does not ask for Pienso que

old: Keep *porque* separate from *para que*: *porque* gives the reason something already happened, while *para que* expresses a purpose or goal — don't reach for *para que* when you are simply explaining why.
new: Tell the story in order: what happened, then the reason with *porque*, the result with *por eso*, and your opinion with *pienso que*.
why: the tip brings in para que (subjunctive, Unit 27), which the learner has not met
